explanation: The theorem says Tor_{n+1}(X, Y) vanishes when the first argument X is zero. Mathlib's `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Tor.lean` has only `isZero_Tor_succ_of_projective` and `isZero_Tor'_succ_of_projective`, which give vanishing when an argument is projective, not when it is zero. `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/LeftDerived.lean` has only `Functor.isZero_leftDerived_obj_projective_succ`. I found no lemma that the left-derived functor of a zero functor is zero, nor any `Additive` or `PreservesZeroMorphisms` instance for `Tor C n`; either would have allowed a one-line `Functor.map_isZero` argument. The group-homology `Tor` in RepresentationTheory likewise has only the projective version. The current proof relies on the library's own `torLES_torIso`.
